leverage.exposure: The balance is negative and the position is leveraged. This is not new, has been open for several runs, and is fully covered by the standing sale, which on its own returns the balance to positive with the squad still legal at eleven. What matters is only that it is unwound before the matchday locks, because a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday. The lock is more than a week away, so there is no time pressure this run — but the deficit is the reason the sale is unconditional, and it is the one thing that must not be forgotten. A negative balance costs nothing at any other moment, so it is not by itself a reason to decline a buy or a flip; the constraint is always whether a position can be unwound by the lock, never the mere existence of the deficit.

binding_gap: Defence, and it is a gap created by the unwind rather than one that exists today. Selling Treu forces the Mainz youngster into a fielded defensive slot at a scoring average far below everyone else in the eleven. That hole is real and known, and it has now been checked against the live board twice: there is no defender available who both improves on it and survives the unwind arithmetic. It is therefore an accepted cost, not an open problem, and future runs should not re-derive it from scratch.

verdict.detail: Nothing has changed in the two hours since the last run, and no action is urgent. sell.reason: Treu, unconditional and unchanged. He is the lowest-scoring player in the fielded eleven and simultaneously the largest single sale that clears the deficit in one leg, so he is both the cheapest points sacrifice and the most efficient unwind — a combination no alternative matches. Dated news confirms he is fit, uninjured after his Germany debut, and named in Freiburg's probable eleven for matchday five, so this is a sale made on structure, not on fitness. On timing: selling back to Kickbase pays exactly the market value with no spread, and he is on a rising trend, so the proceeds grow with each daily update he is held through. The earliest sensible moment is comfortably after tonight's update has propagated — a previously measured sell-back showed the new value does not take effect the instant the update fires, and can lag by up to roughly twenty minutes. Holding him longer than that is not a mistake while the trend stays positive; the only thing that must not happen is arriving at the lock with the position still open.

killed_this_run.name: Leopold Querfeld
killed_this_run.why:
KILLED ON ARITHMETIC SO NO RUN RE-DERIVES HIM. He is the single most tempting listing on the board this run and the only genuine points upgrade anywhere on it: DEF, ap 144, st 0, mvt 1, against Treu's ap 76 in the fielded slot Treu is about to vacate. He still fails, twice over.

(1) HE CANNOT BE UNWOUND, WHICH IS THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY BINDS. Manager ask from Borussia Rumpelfuss, listed 2026-09-30T15:05:56Z, prc 15.000.000 against mv 12.580.331. Buying takes cash from -10.773.918 to -25.773.918 and the squad to 13, which permits exactly TWO sales before the 11-man floor. The two largest sellable bodies are Treu 12.818.870 and Deman 10.806.960 = 23.625.830, which leaves the balance at -2.148.088. A negative balance at the MD5 start scores ZERO for the entire matchday. There is no third sale that keeps eleven players, so the position is unwindable only by breaking the floor. This is a hard kill, not a price quibble.

(2) EVEN AT mv HE IS POINTS-NEGATIVE, WHICH IS THE SURPRISE AND THE REASON TO LOG IT. Suppose the ask came down to mv 12.580.331: cash -23.354.249 against the same 23.625.830 of unwind = +271.581, so it barely clears. But the unwind now costs Deman (ap 101) as well as Treu (ap 76), and the squad lands at 11, which forces Nakuzola (ap 27) into the XI. Fielded ap goes 1353 -> 1353 - 76 - 101 + 144 + 27 = 1347. That is SIX POINTS WORSE for 12,6M of churn. The ap 144 headline is an illusion created by the two bodies it takes to pay for him.

(3) THE PRICE IS OUTSIDE EVERY MEASURED BAND ANYWAY. +19,24% over mv on a MANAGER ASK, against a measured manager-to-manager clearing band of +3,06% to +4,35%, widened only to +6,62% by the Stiller clear (H53duk0). That is roughly 3x the top of the band, and a manager ask is seller's choice, not an auction, so there is no contest to lose by refusing. Nothing above +6,62% has ever cleared manager-to-manager in this league.

REVERSAL: require ALL of: the ask AT OR BELOW mv; the squad at 13 or more so his purchase does not consume two fielded bodies; and a recomputed fielded-ap delta that is POSITIVE after counting whoever actually funds him. Being ap 144 is NOT a reversal - that was already true when he was killed.

movers.reason: Two qualifying candidates now, not one. Both are true Kickbase board listings with no manager attached, both priced at exactly market value, both on the rising trend flag, and both clean on the transfer check that a pure value flip requires — neither has any dated news suggesting he might leave the league. Bid exactly market value on each and never raise; chasing either into the contested cluster destroys the edge outright. Neither needs a starter check, and the second one in particular has a poor scoring average and a bench role that are deliberately irrelevant here — fitness does not enter the daily value tick, and he must not be mistaken for a points buy. One structural caveat that applies to both and had not been recorded before: each listing expires after two daily updates rather than before the next one, so a bid fixed at today's value will sit several percent below the value that applies when the auction actually clears. That cuts the chance of winning appreciably while raising the margin if it does win. The correct response is to treat these as cheap lottery tickets rather than high-probability flips, and emphatically not to raise in compensation. Capital for both together is a small fraction of spending power, and either can be unwound in a single sale long before the lock. The drift table was re-measured from the event log this run and is essentially unchanged from the stored figures on a materially larger sample, so there is still no sign of rivals crowding into this edge. The two open questions stand: it is still unknown whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap how many flips can run at once, and the edge remains measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals pile in.
